clue.text: Man keeps on in charge with victory on satellite TV - perhaps, yes, I can now milk a scandal

definitions.text: yes, I can now milk a scandal
definitions.note: a cryptic description: words the woman at the centre of the scandal might say

indicators.note: a word that keeps something holds it inside itself

blocks.note: a man is a male
taken as written
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge
a victory is a win
Sky is the British satellite television company

explanation.surface: A tabloid boasts of its satellite TV scoop while a woman at the centre of a scandal plans to cash in on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonus: 'yes I can now milk' is itself an exact rearrangement of the name. Monica Lewinsky was the White House intern in President Clinton's 1998 scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: The White House intern later profited from her notoriety through a book and television interviews, so the boast fits her.

clue.text: Was 8's thing the result of l-lemon due in MMI?

indicators.note: a result is what comes out after the letters have been worked over and rearranged

blocks.note: the stammered l, lemon, due, in and the Roman numerals MMI, all letters kept

explanation.surface: A mocking question: was the minister's pet project just a botched lemon delivered in 2001?
explanation.walkthrough: MMI is 2001 in Roman numerals, and a lemon is a dud. Peter Mandelson, the answer to 8, was the minister in charge of the Millennium Dome, the London exhibition that opened in 2000 and flopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandelson oversaw the London exhibition building in Greenwich as minister, so it was his project, which became a famous political embarrassment.

clue.text: ... then grandad's the Queen in China!

definitions.note: a place in China rather than a word for China

blocks.note: in grandad's household his queen is grandma, Nan
if Nan is the queen, grandad is her king

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: grandad, absurdly, turns out to be the Queen, in China of all places.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 1 down. Nan is British slang for a grandmother; as the queen of the house she makes grandad the king, giving Nan King.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanking, now usually spelt Nanjing, is a major city and former capital in eastern China.

clue.text: Egyptologist eating swan and chips

indicators.note: whoever is eating something takes it inside, so one word goes into the other

blocks.note: Howard Carter, who found Tutankhamun's tomb
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: An archaeologist is pictured tucking into a meal of swan with chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' looks like the side order but is the definition: Chips is the traditional British nickname for a carpenter, as in a ship's carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a woodworker is nicknamed Chips, from the wood shavings his trade produces, especially aboard ship.

clue.text: Plant grown wild in Luton not functioning

indicators.note: on means functioning, so not functioning tells us to take on away
wild letters run free and do not stay in their printed order

blocks.note: taken as written
the town's name with ON removed

explanation.surface: A weed sprouts untended in Luton, a town where nothing seems to work.
explanation.walkthrough: Luton is a town north of London. 'Grown wild' reads as the plant's habit but supplies the letters and the signal to rearrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lungwort is a woodland herb with spotted leaves, once used to treat chest complaints, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Laid to show war heartless and death a non-starter

indicators.note: without a heart, the word loses its central letter
something that never starts is missing its opening letter

blocks.note: the word with its middle letter dropped
the word with its first letter dropped

explanation.surface: Something is laid at a memorial to show how cruel war is and how death came too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a whole like a Remembrance scene; the definition is the opening phrase describing what is laid at a memorial to show respect.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath of flowers is placed at a grave or memorial as a mark of respect, so it is something set down for display.

clue.text: Dare in strip lifting Irish bottom

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting lets the letters climb, so they read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Dan Dare, the space hero of the Eagle comic strip
Ir is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: Someone is dared to strip off, ending up baring an Irish bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Dare, Pilot of the Future, was a classic British comic-strip hero from the 1950s Eagle, so the 'Dare' in a strip is Dan.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, so it serves as a synonym for the very bottom of something.

clue.text: Clever clogs is King of Berlin since 1989?

blocks.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess
the Berlin Wall fell in 1989, so since then the city has had no wall

explanation.surface: Is the smart alec the ruler of the German capital since reunification?
explanation.definitionFit: Clever clogs is British slang for someone who shows off what they know, which is what a smug know-it-all does.

clue.text: MP entered loans foolishly?

indicators.note: acting foolishly means acting in a muddled way, so these letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: all fourteen letters kept

explanation.surface: Did a member of parliament unwisely take out loans?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: in 1998 Peter Mandelson resigned from the Cabinet over an undeclared home loan from a fellow minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour politician resigned from government in 1998 after failing to declare a large private home loan from colleague Geoffrey Robinson.

clue.text: Capital halved for the farm, extending some time into the future

definitions.text: extending some time into the future

indicators.note: halved means cut in two, so only the first half of the word is kept

blocks.note: half of LONDON, the capital
a grange is a farmhouse with its outbuildings

explanation.surface: A city split in two to make room for farming, with plans stretching far ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-range forecast or plan looks well ahead in time, covering a distant period rather than the near term.

clue.text: A bee's purpose: to carry the gold back

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it, so one word goes inside the other
going back means the combined letters run from right to left

blocks.note: an end is an aim or purpose
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A bee's whole job is to bring the golden nectar home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bee's purpose' sounds like one phrase, but 'A bee' is the definition and ''s' means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a male honeybee, whose only role is mating with the queen, so it is one kind of bee.

clue.text: Send off team's inside half?

indicators.note: inside places one part within the other

blocks.note: the first half of ELEVEN, the team written as a word
a football or cricket team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A referee sends off the team's inside half, a midfield position in football.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the trick: a team can be written as the word eleven or as Roman numerals, and the clue uses both.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to banish them from their country, which is a way of sending them away.

clue.text: Sluice that perhaps forced out a president

definitions.text: that perhaps forced out a president

blocks.note: first meaning: a gate controlling the flow of water

blocks.clueFragment: that perhaps forced out a president
blocks.note: second meaning: the 1970s US political scandal

explanation.walkthrough: The 'perhaps' is playful: the scandal certainly drove President Nixon to resign in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluice is a barrier regulating a channel's flow, and the scandal named after an office complex ended Nixon's presidency.

clue.text: Weapon turned on a politician of little value

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a gun is a weapon
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone turns a weapon on a worthless politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory is a formal word meaning trifling, futile or without force, so something nugatory is worth very little.

clue.text: Nothing left in morose "Hobbit" character

indicators.note: in places the first two parts within the third

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
L is the abbreviation for left
glum means gloomy, morose

explanation.surface: A sullen character from The Hobbit, left with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suits the creature itself, left with nothing after losing his precious ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Gollum is the slimy creature in Tolkien's novel from whom Bilbo takes the ring, so he is a figure in that book.

clue.text: Tubes replacing spaghetti with hoops instead of squares

indicators.note: instead of says one set of letters takes the place of another
read as re-placing, putting the letters in new places

blocks.note: taken as written
hoops are round, like the letter O
T-squares, so the two Ts

explanation.surface: Spaghetti hoops, a British tinned pasta, swapped in for square-cut pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: Spaghetti hoops are ring-shaped tinned pasta in Britain. Swap the two Ts of the word for two Os, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Oesophagi, the plural of oesophagus, are the muscular gullets carrying food from throat to stomach, which are tubes.

clue.text: Greek Hades, horribly nice

indicators.note: something done horribly is messed up, so these letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: Hades is the Greek underworld, hell
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry verdict that the Greek underworld is horribly pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellenic is the adjective for the Hellenes, the ancient and modern people of Greece, so it means Greek.

clue.text: Bun baked, or not initially, like the one in the oven?

definitions.text: like the one in the oven?

indicators.note: baking transforms the dough, so these letters are reworked into a new order
initially points to the opening letter only

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
its first letter

explanation.surface: Is the bun baked yet or not? The baker peers into the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bun in the oven' is British slang for a baby on the way, which explains the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby still in the womb, the joking bun in the oven, has not yet been born, so it is not yet delivered.

clue.text: Medicinal element turning stomach in senior clergyman, missing work

indicators.note: missing says a part is lost from the word
turning round makes the word run backwards
in places one part within the other

blocks.note: a bishop is a senior member of the clergy
op, short for opus, is a work
tum is informal for stomach

explanation.surface: A bishop off work with an upset stomach reaches for a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Op, short for opus, is the standard crossword work; tum is British informal for the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bismuth is a metallic chemical element whose compounds are used in indigestion remedies, so it is a medicinal element.

clue.text: All fingers and thumbs collecting snake eggs, a small amount in the kitchen

definitions.text: a small amount in the kitchen

indicators.note: whatever is collecting things gathers them inside itself

blocks.note: fingers and thumbs together number ten
an asp is a venomous snake
eggs are shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A clumsy cook fumbles snake eggs, measuring out a small amount in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All fingers and thumbs' is a British idiom for clumsy, but here it is a count: ten digits.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaspoon is a standard small measure in cooking recipes, roughly five millilitres, so it names a small quantity.

clue.text: Eye expert implanting one into boss-eyed locust

indicators.note: implanting places something inside, so a letter goes into the word
boss-eyed means squinting, seeing things askew, so the letters are skewed

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eye specialist gives a new lens to a cross-eyed insect.
explanation.walkthrough: Boss-eyed is British slang for squinting, a fitting signal in a clue about eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Oculist is an older word for an ophthalmologist or optician, a professional who treats and examines eyes.

clue.text: First shot of rally holds point with bend on ball

indicators.note: whatever holds something keeps it within itself

blocks.note: in tennis a rally begins with a serve
W, west, a compass point

explanation.surface: A tennis player opens the rally with a curling serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First shot of rally' looks like letter selection, but the whole phrase means the shot a tennis rally starts with.
explanation.definitionFit: Swerve is the curl a player puts on a kicked or thrown ball so it bends in flight.

clue.text: Denial of responsibility avoids law being broken

indicators.note: something broken falls into pieces that can be put together differently

blocks.note: all nine letters kept

explanation.surface: Someone dodges blame when caught breaking the law.
explanation.definitionFit: A disavowal is a refusal to acknowledge something, especially to accept blame or connection, so it is a repudiation.

clue.text: Gore has valid application

indicators.note: an application puts something to new use, here working the letters into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Al Gore has made a valid application, perhaps for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious Gore is the US vice-president; the one meant is the American novelist Gore Vidal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore Vidal was an American novelist and essayist, so his first name points to his surname.

clue.text: Cut fruit

blocks.note: first meaning: trim back branches
second meaning: a dried plum

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like slicing fruit; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners trim shrubs back to encourage growth, and a dried plum carries the same name.

clue.text: Hillock discovered after initial sex change?

indicators.note: a sex change turns female into male, applied here only to the opening letter

blocks.note: discovered means found

explanation.surface: A mound turned up after a sex-change operation, an absurd medical find.
explanation.walkthrough: F stands for female and M for male, so the change swaps the first letter of FOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound is a small rounded heap of earth, the same as a little hill.

clue.text: Welsh minister with a sin drove off the rails?

indicators.note: a train off the rails is wrecked and scattered, so these letters are disordered

blocks.note: all nine letters kept

explanation.surface: A sinning minister in Wales was driven to go off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: Ron Davies was Secretary of State for Wales who resigned in 1998 after what he called a 'moment of madness' on Clapham Common, a park in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Ron Davies served as Labour's Secretary of State for Wales in the British Cabinet until his 1998 resignation.

clue.text: Neglected issue in the 1 across affair

definitions.text: Neglected issue in the 1 across affair

blocks.note: surface reading: a matter overlooked amid the scandal
setter's reading: issue means offspring, the president's daughter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' is the crossword word for a child. The president's daughter was a teenager when her father's affair with the intern became public.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the only child of Bill and Hillary Clinton, a family member arguably overlooked during her father's 1998 scandal.
